correctness.rationale: On full tensor Fock space and any nonzero complex Hilbert space H, grade-wise norm triangle inequality yields ||P_{≤N}(ℓ(u)+ℓ(v)^*)P_{≤N}||≤||B_N(a,b)||, where B has downward off-diagonal a=||u||, upward b=||v||. Splitting scalar input coordinates by parity, each block has a nonnegative maximizing vector. For either input parity the explicitly alternating unit pure-tensor words with successive left letters uhat/vhat yield the exact two neighboring output terms a ξ_{j+1}+b ξ_{j−1} aligned grade-wise. Hence both parity-block upper bounds are attained and the norm equals ||B|| independent of angle/dimension. N=0 yields 0, a=0 or b=0 yields max(a,b). B*B consists of two Jacobi blocks with diagonal a²1_{j<N}+b²1_{j>0} and second off-diagonals ab. For a=b=s it is the path adjacency matrix, norm 2s cos(π/(N+2)), loss sπ²/(N+2)²+O(s/(N+2)^4). Independent full finite-tensor matrices for d=2, N=1..4 and three complex direction pairs reproduced all scalar norms and balanced cosine values. Infinite-dimensional statement is from constructive proof, not finite numerics.
